newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom confirms Saturn interconnect deal.
newsitem.headline: Telecom confirms Saturn interconnect deal.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand and cable TV company Saturn on Friday signed an interconnect agreement which paves the way for a significant new entrant to roll out in the residential service market here.
Saturn, formerly Kiwi Cable, is controlled UIH Asia/Pacific Communications Inc, a unit of United International Holdings Inc.
Saturn is this year rolling out its cable network in Wellington after conducting a three-year pilot programme south of the capital, and aims to pass 500,000 homes in three to five years.

Company executives told reporters the fibre-based technology would allow Saturn to offer a portfolio of services from cable video through telephony to high-speed data connections and a new digital-based home movie on-demand service.
It has plans to invest up to NZ$600 million developing its cable network over the life of a 10-year business plan which sees expansion into the cities of Christchurch and Auckland.
Telecom also operates a cable TV network, First Media, and plans to roll out cable in Auckland and Wellington.

"Within 18 months we will have completed the construction of our network in the Wellington region and we will be competing intensely against Telecom for customers," Saturn chief executive Jack Matthews told a news conference.
Saturn says it envisages a large part of its future revenues will come from providing residential telephone services.
